> > >
> > > We just checked in a change to the GitHub repository that should improve things quite a bit. I'm not sure this will be our final solution to this problem, but welcome your feedback.
> > >
> > > The change is a new function called "isolate", and it lets you execute code that reads from reactive values/functions, without having their reactivity "infect" the caller.
> > >
> > > So a reactive data frame that only recalculates itself when an action button (with the id "recalcButton") is pressed might look like this:
> > >
> > > mydata <- reactive(function() {
> > >   # Don't do anything until after the first button push.
> > >   if (input$recalcButton == 0)
> > >     return(NULL)
> > >
> > >   # Note that just by virtue of checking the value of input$recalcButton,
> > >   # we're now going to get called whenever it is pushed.
> > >
> > >   return(isolate({
> > >     # Now do the expensive stuff
> > >     foo <- activateInterlock(input$foo)
> > >     bar <- connectDynotherm(input$bar)
> > >     baz <- bringInfracellsUp(input$baz)
> > >     c(foo=foo, bar=bar, baz=baz)
> > >   }))
> > > })
> > >
> > > So mydata will automatically react to changes in recalcButton (i.e. when it is pushed) but not to changes in the inputs foo, bar, or baz.
> > >
> > > How to install
> > >

messages.subject: onclick vs onchange
messages.subject_clean: onclick vs onchange
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have a few radio buttons (just as well could have been dropdown list). It is hooked up to Shiny through a reactive function on server side. When the user clicks on a radio button, shiny goes ahead and changes the reactivePrint output as it is hooked up to the reactive input function.

This all works fine. However what I really want to do is uncheck the radio buttons to have nothing selected between clicks. I am doing that now using onclick javascript on each radio button input.

Now to the issue:

1. User clicks option B
2. shiny reacts and shows the output for option B in reactivePrint
3. js resets radio to have nothing checked. Now no option is selected.
4. User clicks option B again, nothing happens.
5. User clicks any other option (say option A), now shiny reacts and shows the output for option A in reactivePrint

The problem is that user has to click a different value the next time for this to work. They cannot click the same value. This is probably because shiny is looking for changes in the radio button. And since the value now is the same as before, it thinks there is no change.

In other words, I want to reset the value of the input between displays of output.

Thanks

messages.body_plain:
Right now, only the $<- operator is defined for the output object, but we'll soon be adding the [[<- operator, so you can do things like:
  output[['plot']] <- stuff

I don't think it'll possible to assign a list directly to output, as you did, but it should be possible for you to write a wrapper function that takes a list and then assigns each item in the list to output (using `output[[x]] <- y`), as in:
  setOutput(list(plot = aa, table = bb))

-Winston

messages.subject: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
messages.subject_clean: data.frame with one row converted to object of primitives in JSON
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

  I am sending data frames in JSON format to the browser client.

  Usually a data frame is transferred as an JSON object of arrays.

  In the special case where there is only one row, the JSON is an object of primitives

This seems to be the default behaviour of TOJSONIO::toJSON

> library(RJSONIO)
> d=data.frame(a=1:2,b=letters[3:4])
> cat(toJSON(d[1,]))
{
 "a": 1,
"b": "c"
}
> cat(toJSON(d))
{
 "a": [ 1, 2 ],
"b": [ "c", "d" ]
}

This transformation is equivalent to the 'drop'=T argument to the `[` operator, but

I have addressed this on the server side using a function:

    forceTableVector = function(table) {
      lapply(as.list(table),as.list)
    }

But toJSON has an argument to do this:

> asIs:
> a logical value that, if TRUE causes R vectors of length 1 to be represented as arrays in JSON, but if FALSE to be represented as scalars, where appropriate (i.e. not the top level of the JSON content). This avoids having to explicitly mark sub-elements in an R object as being of class AsIs.

> cat(toJSON(d[1,],asIs=T))
{
 "a": [ 1 ],
"b": [ "c" ]
}

But perhaps shiny could make this transformation the default (especially while it's still beta!)

Note that the asIS `I()` function does not help here:

> cat(toJSON(I(d[1,])))
{
 "a": 1,
"b": "c"
}

But an alternative formulation of the forceTable function is suggested by this:

> cat(toJSON(lapply(d[1,],I)))
{
 "a": [ 1 ],
"b": [ "c" ]
}

-Alex Brown

  cars

messages.subject: Shiny 0.3.0 released
messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.3.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We've released Shiny 0.3.0, and it's available on CRAN now. Glimmer will be updated with the latest version of Shiny some time later today.

To update your installation of Shiny, run:
  install.packages('shiny')

Highlights of the new version include:

* Some bugs were fixed in `reactivePrint()` and `reactiveText()`, so that they have slightly different rules for collecting the output. Please be aware that some changes to your apps' text output is possible. The help pages for these functions explain the behavior.

* New `runGitHub()` function, which can run apps directly from a repository on GitHub

* New `runUrl()` function, which can run apps stored as zip or tar files on a remote web server.

* New `isolate()` function, which allows you to access reactive values (from input) without making the function dependent on them.

* Improved scheduling of evaluation of reactive functions, which should reduce the number of "extra" times a reactive function is called.

For examples illustrating how to use runGitHub() and runUrl(), see:
  https://github.com/rstudio/shiny_example

For a full list of changes, see:
  http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/shiny/NEWS

-Winston

deploy:

   rsync -avz --delete <local-repo> <username>@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Error
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server Error
messages.body_plain:
In an ideal world, you could simply speed up the startup of your app. One way to do this is to perform all the data loading/calculating logic once, and use save() or save.image() to save part or all of your global environment to an .RData file, and load that .RData file on startup of your Shiny app (in global.R).

In case that is not possible for whatever reason, I have implemented some additional config options to allow you to configure the amount of time Shiny Server will wait for your app to start up. It is on a branch though, I need to wait for code review and testing to merge it into the main repo. In the meantime you can install it with:

sudo npm install -g https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny-server/archive/configurable-timeouts.tar.gz

Josh told me about your case over e-mail and it sounds like not only would you want to have very long timeouts on startup, but also, to keep the app running even after all users leave so you don't have to pay that long startup cost again when a new user logs on. That is configurable in this build as well.

The two new config file directives are called startup_timeout and shutdown_delay. A value of -1 will make either value infinite; a positive float will be interpreted as number of seconds.

In case you have not created a config file and are just using the default, you want your config file to look like this:

> run_as shiny;
> startup_timeout -1;
> shutdown_delay -1;
>
> server {
>   listen 3838;
>
>   location / {
>     site_dir /var/shiny-server/www;
>     log_dir /var/shiny-server/log;
>     directory_index on;
>   }
> }

Hope that helps.

Hello to the Shiny team,

All the best,
Andy

On Thursday, 8 November 2012 18:33:07 UTC-6, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Sorry, I think we forgot to document this--we have serious compatibility issues with IE9 and below. That's a pretty big oversight, we'll try to correct that soon.
> IE8 currently doesn't work with either Shiny running locally, or Shiny server (e.g. our live example apps on the Shiny homepages).
> IE9 currently doesn't work with Shiny running locally, but it does work with Shiny server.
> IE10 should work fine with both versions of Shiny.
> If you can install Chrome Frame <http://www.google.com/chromeframe> for IE (any supported version), then both versions of Shiny will work.
> Please let us know if this is a problem for you, including what version of IE you need support for, and whether it's an option for your users to install a more up-to-date browser. If IE compatibility is really going to stop adoption of Shiny in companies then we would consider tackling the quite significant engineering tasks needed to solve these compatibility issues. But of course that means time we couldn't spend improving the rest of the framework. So we definitely need your feedback to help us prioritize.
>
> (In case you are interested in the technical details, Shiny relies heavily on a feature of HTML5 called Websockets. IE8 and 9 don't support websockets; Microsoft used to have a free plugin for IE9 that enabled websocket support, but they seem to have pulled it down since IE10 was released. Shiny server works around this limitation by using communication platforms from other languages (that isn't available in R) that it translates to/from websocket traffic. That's why IE9 works on Shiny server but not locally. IE8 doesn't even work on Shiny server because of a different, unrelated issue <http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3586749/how-to-get-around-ie8-32k-limit-on-datauri-on-base64-encode>.)
>
> Thanks for the question!

messages.subject_clean: Assigning the value of numericInput depending on a radioButton or selectList choice
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I'm trying to put together a system where, upon the choice of an item from a selectList or radioButton, the values of some numericInput are altered, hence causing everything depending on that to be re-executed.

I thought the right way to do this would be to use the conditionalPanel in this way:

> > selectInput(inputId='Physiology', label='Choose a species/physiology', choices=c('Rat','Mouse'), multiple=F, selected='Rat'),
> >     shiny::conditionalPanel(
> >       condition="input.Physiology == 'Rat'",
> >       numericInput("GI_length", "GI_length (m):", .1, step=.1),
> >       numericInput("GI_radius", "GI_radius (m):", .0018, step=.0001),
> >       numericInput("GI_TrTime", "GI_TrTime (mins):", 5)
> >     ),
> >     shiny::conditionalPanel(
> >       condition="input.Physiology == 'Mouse'",
> >       numericInput("GI_length", "GI_length (m):", .04, step=.01),
> >       numericInput("GI_radius", "GI_radius (m):", .0006, step=.0001),
> >       numericInput("GI_TrTime", "GI_TrTime (mins):", 15)
> >     ),

However, although this gives me the kind of interface I am looking for, it doesn't work since the reactivity is attached only to the first instance of the different numericInput with the same inputId. The model re-evaluates correctly when the 'rat' option is selected, in the specific case, and I modify any of the three numericInput. However, if I select 'Mouse', and change the values in that panel, nothing happens.

Any suggestions on how to get out of this impasse? Is there a way to 'write' values to a numericInput in a reactive way, depending from the choice of a selectList? So that I can export them out of the conditionalPanel, and avoid having more than one with the same inputID?

Thanks for any feedback,

> Luca

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server Error
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server Error
messages.body_plain:
Regarding the slow load issue: if the slow part involves loading and/or processing a large data set, and if the data is common to each user session, you can restructure your code so that it is run once, when the Shiny app is started, instead of each time a user connects.

For example:

# A read-only data set that will load once, when Shiny starts, and will be
# available to each user session
bigDataSet <- read.csv('bigdata.csv')

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  # Runs each time someone starts a session
  anotherDataSet <- read.csv('otherdata.csv')

})

See this page for more information about scoping:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

-Winston

messages.subject_clean: Assigning the value of numericInput depending on a radioButton or selectList choice
messages.body_plain:
The issue is that conditionalPanels are merely hidden when the condition is false. So both the Rat and Mouse conditionalPanel are always on the web page - it's just that one of them is visible.

If you're using Chrome, you can inspect the structure of the web page by right-clicking on the element and selecting "Inspect Element". I've attached an image of what it looks like when inspecting your page. As you can see, both Mouse and Rat are there.

To work around it, you can use dynamic UI. For an example, see:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/dynamic_ui/
Source code at:
  https://gist.github.com/4211337

And the tutorial page at:
  http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#dynamic-ui

-Winston

You can use HTML in Shiny apps in several ways. 1) Inside of sidebarPanel and mainPanel, you can insert arbitrary HTML expressions using R code. See the ?tags help topic for details and examples. Here is an example reflecting

bar

p(img(src="foo"), "bar") If you need a tag whose name is not explicitly exported, you can use the tags object which contains all valid HTML tags (that we know about today). For example the previous example could equally have been written as: tags$p(tags$img(src="foo"), "bar") 2) Inside of sidebarPanel and mainPanel, you can also include literal HTML strings by using the HTML function, for example: HTML('

bar

') 3) You can put HTML in a separate file, and from sidebarPanel or mainPanel you can use the includeHTML function. messages.subject: Shiny 0.3.1
messages.subject_clean: Shiny 0.3.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone -

We have a new version of Shiny, 0.3.1, with a fix for the file downloading bug. It's not on CRAN, since the CRAN maintainers prefer not to have new releases more than once a month. But you can install it on your local machine by using devtools, and we will update Glimmer to version 0.3.1 shortly.

If you'd like to install the new version on your machine, do the following:

# Install devtools if needed (note that a new version of devtols, 1.0, was just released)
install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github('shiny', 'rstudio', 'v0.3.1')

In addition to the download fix, the following changes are in 0.3.1:

* You an now do double-bracket assignment with output, as in `output[['foo']] <- xx`
* Reactive functions now preserve the visible/invisible state of their returned values.

-Winston

Below a set of ui specifications I added. I don't have anything for numer input but hopefully the below will help you get started. The first line puts radio buttons side-by-side (thanks Joe). If you figure out how to do this with numeric inputs please post back.

To adjust the height of a specific multiple-select:
tags$style(type='text/css', "#columns { height: 200px; padding-bottom: 35px;}"),

To adjust a textinput:
tags$style(type='text/css', "#dv_select { max-width: 185px; }"),

Haven't found the class name to change this for the whole app. I tried 'text' but that didn't work.

 sidebarPanel(

      tags$head(
        tags$style(type="text/css", "label.radio { display: inline-block; }", ".radio input[type=\"radio\"] { float: none; }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", "select { max-width: 200px; }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", "textarea { max-width: 185px; }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", "text { width: 15px; !important }"),
        tags$style(type="text/css", ".jslider { max-width: 200px; }"),
        tags$style(type='text/css', ".well { max-width: 310px; }"),
        tags$style(type='text/css', ".span4 { max-width: 310px; }")
      ),
